newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close at another record high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close at another record high.

text.p: The Australian share market ended at its second successive record closing high on Wednesday.
Bank shares continued their recent strong run as investors tipped higher dividends ahead of the latest round of results.
The All Ordinaries index ended 4.8 points up at 2,517.6, building on Tuesday's previous record finish with A$956 million (US$741 million) worth of trade going through the market.
But brokers said a fall in the futures and weaker bonds pointed to a possible drop in the All Ordinaries on Thursday.
The fresh record high set on Wall Street underpinned the market rise, despite a shaky start, brokers said.
"The consistency in the Dow is giving our market consistency. It is not being generated by us, it is coming from overseas," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at Intersuisse.
Banks were finding good support and ignored the fall in the bond market, brokers said.

Oil group Woodside was the strongest riser amongst the blue chips on vague talks that its major shareholder Anglo-Dutch oil giant, Shell/Royal Dutch Group, was going to buy the rest of the group out, brokers said.

Market heavyweight BHP saw the largest value of trade with about A$174 million going through the market or just under 20 percent of total market trading value, the buying interest helped the group recover some recent losses.
John Fairfax shares fell as rumours of a quick takeover for the newspaper group waned on political opposition to a bid for the publisher, particularly from Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting.
Base metals miner Pasminco attracted buying after the giant Century Zinc project got the go-ahead. Pasminco has agreed to buy the project from Anglo-Australian miner RTZ-CRA.
